case-overview.analysisPrompt: Review this document and extract all available company identification and investment basics: company name, full legal name if available, what the company does (short plain-English description of the product/service, the target customer, and the core problem solved), sector/industry, founding year, headquarters location, estimated team size, stage (Pre-seed/Seed/Series A/Series B/Growth), capital requirement or ask amount, stated valuation, opportunity type (e.g. B2B SaaS/Marketplace/DeepTech/ClimateTech), any mentioned website URL, and a one-sentence business model summary. Extract concrete evidence for each field found, note any contradictions, and estimate a 0-10 score based on the completeness and quality of company information in the document.
case-overview.summaryPrompt:
Update the Case Overview canonical document. Instead of a markdown summary, output the summary field as a VALID JSON object (no markdown wrapping, no code fences — just raw JSON) with this exact structure:
{
  "companyName": "Full company name or null",
  "tagline": "One-sentence company tagline or null",
  "description": "2-3 sentence plain-English description of what the company does, who the customer is, and the core problem solved. No jargon.",
  "sector": "Industry/sector string or null",
  "stage": "Pre-seed | Seed | Series A | Series B | Growth | null",
  "foundedYear": "YYYY string or null",
  "headquarters": "City, Country or null",
  "teamSize": "Team size string (e.g. '12' or '<20') or null",
  "website": "URL if found in documents or null",
  "businessModel": "One sentence on how they make money or null",
  "capitalRequirement": "Capital ask string (e.g. €2M) or null",
  "statedValuation": "Valuation string or null",
  "opportunityType": "Opportunity type (e.g. B2B SaaS) or null",
  "investmentRationale": "One-sentence investment thesis from the documents or null"
}
Rules: Keep all fields evidence-based. Use null for any unknown value. Do not add markdown wrapping or code fences. Use wording Data not Canonical Package.
case-overview.webAnalysisPrompt: Search the web to find and verify the company mentioned in the canonical document. Priority tasks in order: 1) Find the official company website — capture their tagline, product description, and any highlighted traction metrics. 2) Search for recent news or press coverage about the company (last 12 months). 3) Look up the company on Crunchbase, LinkedIn, or similar platforms to confirm founding date, team size, investor backing, and funding history. 4) Search for any product launches, case studies, customer references, or notable milestones. Include the official website URL prominently at the top of your summary markdown. Focus on identity verification and web presence — not market analysis.

team-execution.analysisPrompt: Review this document only for leadership quality, team completeness, hiring needs, delivery capability, governance, execution signals, and founder-market fit. Extract concrete evidence, note contradictions, and estimate a 0-10 section score based only on the document.
team-execution.webAnalysisPrompt: Search the web for information about the founders, key executives, and team members mentioned in the canonical document. Look for LinkedIn profiles, professional backgrounds, previous companies, exits, or failures. Verify claimed experience, education credentials, and notable achievements. Search for any press coverage, conference talks, open-source contributions, or industry recognition. Identify red flags such as lawsuits, negative press, short tenures, or pattern of failed ventures. Assess the overall team credibility and execution capability based on web evidence.

business-potential-market.analysisPrompt: Review this document only for market size, growth, urgency of the problem, buyer pain, willingness to pay, competition, distribution, and business model durability. Extract concrete evidence and estimate a 0-10 section score from the document.
business-potential-market.summaryPrompt: Update the Business Potential and Market canonical document in markdown. Explain market attractiveness, go-to-market readiness, competition, monetization strength, and unresolved commercial risks. Refresh the cumulative score using all processed evidence.
business-potential-market.webAnalysisPrompt: Search the web for evidence, market data, competitor information, and industry analysis related to the company and market described in the canonical document. Validate or challenge the claims made about market size, growth rates, competitive landscape, and business model. Find recent news, funding rounds, market reports, and analyst opinions. Identify emerging competitors and industry trends that may impact the investment thesis.

product-technology.analysisPrompt: Review this document only for product differentiation, roadmap credibility, technical moat, data advantage, IP, architecture, security, AI claims, and implementation maturity. Extract concrete evidence and estimate a 0-10 section score from the document.
product-technology.summaryPrompt: Update the Product & Technology canonical document in markdown. Summarize product strengths, technical proof points, scalability concerns, product gaps, and technical diligence follow-ups. Refresh the cumulative score using all processed evidence.
product-technology.webAnalysisPrompt: Search the web for information about the product and technology described in the canonical document. Look for product reviews, user feedback, app store ratings, G2/Capterra reviews, and customer testimonials. Search for the technology stack, open-source repositories, developer documentation, and API references. Verify claimed technical capabilities, patents, or IP. Compare with competing products and technologies — find benchmark comparisons, feature matrices, and analyst reports. Identify any tech debt signals, security vulnerabilities, or scalability concerns mentioned online. Search for the company's presence in developer communities, tech blogs, and conference presentations.

economics-finance.analysisPrompt: Review this document only for revenue quality, unit economics, margins, burn, runway, fundraising need, capital efficiency, forecast credibility, and financial controls. Extract concrete evidence and estimate a 0-10 section score from the document.
economics-finance.summaryPrompt: Update the Economics and Finance canonical document in markdown. Summarize business economics, quality of revenue, margin profile, burn/runway, funding need, financial discipline, and unresolved finance risks. Refresh the cumulative score using all processed evidence.
economics-finance.webAnalysisPrompt: Search the web for financial information about the company described in the canonical document. Look for publicly known funding rounds, valuations, and investor names on Crunchbase, PitchBook, or similar databases. Search for revenue estimates, growth metrics, and financial benchmarks for comparable companies in the same industry and stage. Find industry-standard unit economics benchmarks (CAC, LTV, margins) for this vertical. Verify any claimed financial partnerships, customer contracts, or revenue milestones. Search for market funding environment trends, recent comparable exits or IPOs, and analyst commentary on the sector's financial outlook.

caseSummary.prompt: Read all five canonical Fact Sheet section documents (Case Overview, Team & Execution, Business Potential & Market, Product & Technology, Economics & Finance) and their web analysis results. Synthesize an investment memo snapshot. Return company name, overall score, recommendation, ask amount if stated, stage if inferable, markdown summary, key highlights, key insights, and watchouts. Keep statements evidence-based and explicitly mark unknown values.
